case_source: (From the Judgment and Order dated March 30, 2002 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 4555 of 1999)
full_judgment:
Md Ruhul Amin J : This appeal, by leave, is against the judgment dated March 30, 2002 of a Division Bench of the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 4555 of 1999 making the Rule absolute upon setting aside the judgment and order dated June 23, 1999 of the 3rd Court of Additional District Judge, Bogra in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 74 of 1998 allowing the same in part upon reversing the judgment and order dated October 25, 1998 of the 1st Court of Subordinate Judge (Joint District Judge), Bogra in Arbitration Case No.80 of 1997 dismissing the same.

2. The arbitration case was filed under section 28 of the Acquisition and Requisition of Immovable Property Ordinance, 1982 (Ordinance No. II of 1982).

3. Facts, in short, are that land measuring 3.20 acres of Plot Nos.3840 and 9517 recorded in MRR khatian Nos. 6 and 2077 respectively was acquired in LA Case No. 36 (Shishu Palli) of 1992. The acquiring authority assessed the value of the acquired land at Taka 6,04,000.

4. It is the case of the appellants that although they are the owners of the land so acquired but award has not been prepared in their names, that they approached the authority on March 18, 1993 to pay the amount so assessed in respect of the acquired land but the authority directed the appellants to get their title settled through civil Court since revenue record stands in the name of persons Other that the appellants, that they filed two other application, one on March 30, 1994, and another on April 5, 1994 but compensation assessed was not paid to them and thereupon the appellants filed Other Class Suit No.65 of 1995 seeking declaration of their title in respect of 3.20 acres of land which they purchased on January 11, 1979 from Altaf Ali Chowdhury, that the suit was decreed for 2.90 acres in their favour on May 12, 1996, that in the light of the decree they got their names mutated in the revenue record and thereupon on April 24, 1997 filed petition seeking revision of the award prepared on March 18, 1993 but they had not the desired result, that prayer for revision was rejected on the ground of limitation since the notice of making the award under section 7(1) of the Acquisition and Requisition of Immovable Property Ordinance, 1982 (hereinafter referred to, in brief, the Ordinance) was served on the person interested, on April 24, 1993. In the aforesaid state of the matter the appellants filed the aforementioned Arbitration Case No. 80 of 1997 on June 27, 1997 under section 28 of the Ordinance stating, inter alia, that although they are the owners of the land acquired in LA Case No. 36 of 1992 but the acquiring authority has assessed the compensation in the name of some other persons and further, that although the lands acquired are bhitee land, but the acquiring authority has treated the land as cultivable and fallow land. It was also the case of the appellants that value of the land is Taka 1,58,000 and that market price of per decimal of land is 40,000, that they are running a brick field upon investing Taka 30,00,000, that the appellants in the arbitration case claimed that they are entitled to get the award for an amount of Taka 1,58,00,000 along with 20% additional compensation as provided by law.

5. The arbitration case was contested by the acquiring body as well as by the requiring body by filing separate written objections stating, inter alia, that the arbitration case filed seeking revision of the award is barred by limitation, that upon due compliance of law the notices under sections 3 and 6 of the Ordinance were served on February 8, 1993 and March 1, 1993 respectively, that land measuring 2.90 of Plot No.3840 was recorded in the name of Tohurunnessa-Jebedatun Nessa Waqf Estate and its mutawalli was Mr Mohammad Ali Chowdhury and land measuring 0.30 acre of plot No. 9517 was recorded in the name of Alam Fakir and others, that on physical verification the acquired land was found fallow land, that sale deeds of the preceding 12 months from the date of service of notice under section 3 of the Ordinance were collected and thereupon, Deputy Commissioner assessed the compensation at Taka 1,50,000 per acre in respect of the land of Plot No.3840 and Taka 54,000 in respect of the land of Plot No.9517 with additional compensation. The compensation so assessed stood at Taka 5,76,000 and thereupon notice under section 7(3) of the Ordinance was served on April 24, 1993 and the notice served relating to Plot No. 3840 was received by the Inspector of Waqf, Bogra, that the petitioners (herein appellants) filed application claiming compensation and thereupon Miscellaneous Case No. 11 of 1993 was started, but ultimately, the same was disposed of directing them to get their title settled through civil Court and then they filed suit and got the decree and on the basis thereof got their names mutated in the revenue record, that as per provision of section 28 of the Ordinance the petitioners were required to file petition seeking revision of the award before the Arbitrator with 45 days from the date of service of the notice under section 7(3) of the Ordinance and that although the said notice was served on April 24, 1993 but the Arbitration Case was filed on June 27, 1997 and thus the application for revision of the award was hopelessly barred and, as such, the arbitration case was not maintainable.

6. The arbitrator dismissed the case holding that the compensation assessed is valid, that the petitioners have not proved either by oral or by documentary evidence that value of per decimal of land is Taka 40,000 or that the value of the awarded land is Taka 1,58,00,000 that the award made at Taka 6,04,000 has been made correctly and the award so made does not call for correction.

7. As against the judgment and order of the Arbitrator, the appellants went on appeal. The appellate Court allowed the appeal directing the acquiring body to assess the value of the land at Taka 30,000 per decimal and to pay the awarded compensation within 60 days. Thereupon, the acquiring body moved the High Court Division in revisional jurisdiction and obtained the Rule.

8. The, High Court Division made the Rule absolute on the findings that from the materials on record it appears that notice under section 6 of the Ordinance was served on the persons who were interested in the acquired land, as per record of the Government office and since in the record of the Government names of the petitioners, herein appellants, were not entered, notice was not served on them, that the petitioners knowing about the award filed application on 18-3-1993, i.e. when finally the award was made and that after service of notice of the award under section 7(3) of the Ordinance petitioners filed two applications, one on March 30, 1994 and the other on April 5, 1994 for payment of compensation to them, that after obtaining decree in Other Class Suit No.65 of 1995 the petitioners filed application on April 26, 1997 but awarded money was not paid to them as petitioner's names were not in government record , and in the revenue record and that thereafter, they filed the arbitration case before the Court of Subordinate Judge, Bogra on June 27, 1997 seeking revision of the award, that from the materials on record it is apparent that the petitioners had actual as well as constructive knowledge about the award made by the Deputy Commissioner from date of its preparation, that notice of the award was served upon the persons interested as per record of the Government or that upon the persons known or believed to be interested in the land so acquired, that petitioners ought to have filed the application for revision of award, at least within 45 days from the date of actual knowledge of award, that is from the date when knowing about the award made by the Deputy Commissioner the opposite party Nos. 1 and 2 filed application for getting awarded money", that in the background of the aforesaid facts the application filed before the Arbitrator was barred by limitation, that the opposite parties in the arbitration case specifically stated in the written objection that the arbitration case was barred by limitation and that, in that view of the matter, it could not be said that the petitioners raised the question of the limitation at the time of arguing in this civil revision before this Court for the first time, that failure to frame issue as regard the limitation is not fatal in disposing of the application for revision of award since the procedure laid down in the provision of the Code of Civil Procedure regarding formal determination separately is not enjoined as compulsory in an arbitration proceeding. We have already found that the application for revision of the award has been filed long after the service of notice of the award. The question of limitation in the instant case attracts the jurisdiction of the arbitrator to entertain the application for revision of the award made by the Deputy Commissioner. As the special limitation has been provided in filing such revision so the Arbitrator has no jurisdiction to enlarge the time and to condone the delay in filing application. So, the explanation of delay of filing revision will not improve the position of the opposite party Nos. 1 and 2. In such view of the matter, we are of the view that the Arbitrator and Subordinate Judge, First Court, Bogra ought to have rejected the application for revision of the arbitration in liming and the learned Appellate Court committed a serious error of law in entertaining the time barred application for arbitration. The High Court Division also held that the appellate Court was in error in making direction for revision of the award upon taking the value of per decimal of land at Taka 30,000 since the deeds placing reliance whereon the appellate Court arrived at the view that value of per decimal acquired land is Taka 30,000 are of different mouza or, in other words, the Ext. I series do not relate to the land of the mouza Barbakpur wherein the acquired land situates.

9. Leave was obtained for consideration of the contentions whether the High Court Division was in error in not considering the appellants application for remand of the arbitration case on the ground that Deputy Commissioner while rejecting the prayer for revision of the award placed reliance, on some documents which were not reflecting the correct position, in that land purchased by the appellants was not paddy land but the Deputy Commissioner on some "improper documents" held that the acquired land is paddy land and that Deputy Commissioner did not consider the report of the government pleader which was obtained by the Deputy Commissioner on the appellants' application filed seeking revision of the award, that pursuant to the compromise decree dated May 12, 1996 the appellants' title to the land measuring 2.90 acres of Plot No 3840 listed in MRR Khatian No.6 acquired by the Deputy Commissioner in LA Case No.36 of 1992 was declared and on the basis of the aforesaid decree their names having been mutated in the revenue record and thereby appellants as are interested in the award made by the Deputy Commissioner and that notice under section 7(3) of the Ordinance earlier served on the Inspector of Waqf as was not on the person interested in the award and, that the Deputy Commissioner having had not served any notice of the award on the appellants which is a mandatory requirement under section 7(3) of the Ordinance and, as such, Arbitration Case No.80 of 1997 for revision of the award filed on 27-6-1997 under section 28 of the Ordinance was not barred by limitation and therefore the High Court Division was in error in holding that the arbitration case was barred by limitation as the appellants had knowledge of the award since 18-3-1993 on erroneous interpretation of section 28 of the Ordinance for the purpose of computing the period of limitation for filing the application to the Arbitrator for revision of the award.

10. To appreciate the contentions of the appellants, as are in the leave granting order, certain facts need to be stated. The Deputy Commissioner, Bogra acquired 2.90 acres land of plot No.3840 and 0.30 acre land of plot No. 9517 upon initiating LA Case No.36 (Shishu Palli) of 1992. The undisputed position is that at the time of acquisition of the aforesaid land appellants' names were not in the revenue record or in the record of the Deputy Commissioner. The appellants got their names mutated in the revenue record in 1997 on the basis of the decree passed on 9-5-1996 in other Class Suit No.65 of 1995. The intention to acquire particular land is made known by the Deputy Commissioner to the person(s), interested in the land upon causing publication of notice, under section 3 of the' Ordinance, in the prescribed form and manner "at convenient places on or near the property . . . . . proposed to be acquired". In the instant case the notice under the said section was published on February 8, 1993. After disposal of objection, if any, in the light of the provision of section 4 of the Ordinance, the Deputy Commissioner submits the proposal in the background of the quantity of land going to be acquired to the authority as in section 4(3) of the Ordinance and then if as per provision of section 5 of the Ordinance final decision is made by the authority for the acquisition of the property then in the light of the provision of section 6 of the Ordinance the Deputy Commissioner is required to cause public notice in the prescribed manner at the convenient places on or near the property so going to be acquired expressing the decision of the authority to acquire the property in question and the intention of taking possession thereof and also specifying that claim to compensation for all interest in the property going to be acquired is to be made to the Deputy Commissioner. The notice under section 6 of the Ordinance was served on March 1, 1993. The aforesaid facts are not disputed, by the appellants. As per provision of section 6 of the Ordinance all persons interested in the land acquired would be notified to state the nature of their respective interests in the property and the amount and particulars of their claims to compensation for such interests. Provision of section 6 of the Ordinance also requires serving of notice on the occupier, if any, of the land acquired and all persons known or believed to be interested. therein. The person so notified would be required to make or deliver statement mentioning the name of every other person possessing any interest in the land or any part thereof as co-sharer, mortgagee or otherwise, and of the nature of such interest and profits, if any, received or receivable on account thereof. The appellants after service of notice under section 6 of the Ordinance did neither notify about their interest in the land acquired nor about their claims to the compensation. The Deputy Commissioner in the light of provision of section 7 of the Ordinance after making enquiry into the statement, if any, filed by any person pursuant to the notice given under section 6 of the Ordinance as well as into the value of the property at the date of publication of the notice under section 3 of the Ordinance, and into the respective interests of the parties claiming the compensation shall make an award of the compensation which, in his opinion, shall be allowed for the property and apportion the compensation "among all the persons' known or believed to be interested in the property, of whom, or of whose claims", the Deputy Commissioner has the information. The Deputy Commissioner after making the award of the compensation "shall give immediate notice of the, award to the persons interested". The Deputy Commissioner served the notice under section 7(3) of the Ordinance on 24-4-1993. It may be mentioned award of the compensation was made on 18-3-1993 and 20-3-1993 and thereupon notice under section 7(3) of the Ordinance was served on the aforementioned date.

11. The appellants, as seen from the materials on record, having had information of making of the award of compensation filed a petition on 18-3-1993 to the Deputy Commissioner claiming the compensation but their claim was not entertained since they were not the persons in whose names revenue record stood at that material time, nor their names were in the record of the Deputy Commissioner. It may be mentioned revenue record at the material time i.e. while notices under sections 3, 6 and 7(3) of the Ordinance were served, stood in the name of Tohurunnessa Jebedatun Nessa Waqf Estate in respect of 2.90 acres of Plot No. 3840 and the revenue record in respect of .30 acre of Plot No. 9517 was in the name of Alam Fakir and others. The appellants later on again filed petitions on two other occasions i.e. on 30-3-1994 and 5-4-1994 before the Deputy Commissioner claiming compensation of the acquired land. The Deputy Commissioner while disposing of the petition filed on 30-3-1994 directed the appellants to get their title settled in the civil Court. In that state of the matter the appellants filed Other Class Suit No. 65 of 1995 on. 12-8-1995 and the said suit was decreed on compromise with the Waqf Estate on 12-5-1996 in respect of 2.90 acres of land of Plot No.3840. On the basis of the decree in the aforesaid suit the appellants got their names mutated in the revenue record and thereafter filed the arbitration case on 27-6-1997 seeking revision of the award.

12. Section 28 of the Ordinance provides that any person interested in the compensation, but has not accepted the compensation awarded by the Deputy Commissioner, may within forty-five days from the date of service of notice of the award, i.e. notice under section 7(3) of the Ordinance, file an application to the Arbitrator for revision of the award. As has already been mentioned award was made on 18-3-1993 and the notice of making of the award, as per provision of section 7(3) of the Ordinance, was served on 24-4-1993 in respect of the land measuring 2.90 acre of plot No. 3840 on the Inspector of Waqf, Bogra since revenue record was in the name of the Waqf Estate.

13. The substantive contention of the appellants is that their names having been mutated in the revenue record in the light of the judgment in Other Class Suit No.65 of 1995 and consequently, as they were interested in the award made in the LA Case No.36 of 1992 in respect of 2.90 acres of land of Plot No.3840 and that as the notice under section 7(3) of the Ordinance in respect of 2.90 acres of plot No.3840 served on 24-3-1993 was not on the persons interested in the award or, in other words, on someone other than interested persons (the notice under section 7(3) was served on the Inspector of Waqfs, Bogra) and consequently, any notice of the award in the light of the provision of section 7(3) of the Ordinance having not been served at all on the appellants and, in that state of the matter, arbitration case having been filed on 27-6-1997 as per provision of section 28 of the Ordinance as cannot be considered barred by limitation, the High Court Division was in error in holding that the arbitration case was barred by limitation upon incorrect interpretation of the provision of section 28 of the Ordinance for the purpose of computing the period of limitation for filing the application before the Arbitrator seeking revision of the award and that the High Court Division was in error in holding that the arbitration case was barred by limitation since it was not filed within forty-five days from the date of knowledge of the award.

14. The procedure of acquiring particular land under the Ordinance and the making of award of compensation as well as service of notice of making of the award of compensation in detail have already been stated hereinbefore.

15. The point for determination is, who would be considered person "interested" in the land acquired and the award of compensation from the date of service of notice under section 3 of the Ordinance to the time of making award and service of notice thereof under section 7(1) and 7(3) of the Ordinance respectively.

16. The appellants claimed that they purchased 2.90 acres of land of Plot No. 3840, i.e. one of the plots acquired in LA Case No.36 of 1992, on January 11, 1979 but the fact is that the appellants did not mutate their names in the revenue record till April 26, 1997 and that they got their names mutated in the revenue record after the aforesaid date pursuant to a decree in Other Class Suit No.65 of 1995. So, it is evident that on the date when the notice under section 3 of the Ordinance was served appellants names were not in the revenue record or in any other record of the Government. As mentioned hereinbefore upon preparation of the award of compensation the appellants on 18-3-1993 applied for payment of compensation but the said prayer was not allowed as neither from the Government record nor from the revenue record the appellants were found interested in the land acquired and thereafter on two occasions i.e. on 30-3-1994 and 5-4-1994, appellants' applications were also not entertained. Later on the appellants filed the suit as mentioned hereinabove and obtained decree in respect of 2.90 acres of land of Plot No.3840 and on the basis of the decree got their names mutated in the revenue record in 1997. Provision in section 28 of the Ordinance requires the person(s) interested in the compensation award to file application to the Arbitrator for revision of. the award within 45 days from the date of service of notice of the award under section 7(3) of the Ordinance. Notice of the award was served on the persons, who were found interested in the award, on 24-4-1993. The notice in respect of 2.90 acres of land of Plot No.3840 was served on the Inspector of Waqf since on the relevant date the land stood recorded in the name of Waqf Estate. The appellants after getting their names mutated in the revenue record filed the Miscellaneous Arbitration Case No.80 of 1997 on 27-6-1997 seeking revision of the award.

17. The learned Counsel for the appellants submits that High Court Division was in error in reversing the judgment of the appellate Court upon holding that the arbitration case was barred by limitation, although in spite of the requirement of law no notice of the award was served on the appellants who were interested in the land acquired and consequently, interested in the award made. As seen from the materials on record that notice under section 3 of the Ordinance was served on February 8, 1993 and notice under section 6 of the Ordinance on March 1, 1993. On those dates appellants' names were neither in the revenue record nor in the record of the office of the Deputy Commissioner. It has been contended by the appellants that after their purchase they established brickfield in the land acquired i.e. in the land of Plot No.3840. No material has been brought on record that after service of notice under section 6 of the Ordinance the appellants represented to the Deputy Commissioner about their interest in the property and also the amount of their claim of compensation for such interest. The appellants only appeared in the scene on 18-3-1993 when the award was made under section 7(1) of the Ordinance and thereafter on two other occasions in 1994 as stated hereinbefore.

18. In our opinion, in between the time of initiation of the process of acquisition and the ending thereof with the making of the award of compensation a person is to be considered interested in the acquired property and the award of compensation if his name appears in the revenue record or in the record of the Deputy Commissioner and the Deputy Commissioner while serving notice under section 6 of the Ordinance initially would recognise such person as the person interested in the property going to be acquired and would cause service of notice upon the said person to appear before him to put forward before him nature of his interest in the property and the amount and particulars of his claim to the compensation for such interest. The interest and the claim of other categories of persons as mentioned in section 6 are legally recognisable. Thereafter, upon completion of enquiry as contemplated by section 7(1) of the Ordinance the Deputy Commissioner on making award of compensation would serve notice thereof as required by section 7(3) of the Ordinance on the person(s) found interested in the land acquired as per provision of section 6 of the Ordinance. No material from the side of the appellants has been brought on record to show that although they were occupying the property in question but no notice was served on them as per provision of section 6(2) of the Ordinance. The undisputed position is that when the initial step for acquisition of the property in question was taken and that till the making of the award of compensation in respect of the property so acquired appellants' names were not in the revenue record or in the record of the Deputy Commissioner nor they represented before 18-3-1993 to the Deputy Commissioner about their interest in the award of compensation made in respect of the land so acquired. This being the position the Deputy Commissioner was not required to serve the notice of making of the award of compensation in respect of the land acquired on the appellants.

19. The appellants filed petition on 18-3-1993 seeking payment of compensation but that prayer was rejected since at the stage of the proceeding relating to ascertainment of the interest of persons as per provision of section 6 of the Ordinance they did not represent to the Deputy Commissioner about their interest in the land acquired and in the amount of compensation going to be awarded.

20. Any claim in the acquired land and in the amount of compensation subsequent to the completion of proceeding at the stage of making of award of compensation would only be recognisable on the basis of authoritative material i.e. claim in the compensation is to be supported by the authoritative paper. But claim to the compensation accompanied by authoritative paper would ipso facto not entitle the claimant to have the compensation. The claimant to the compensation is to satisfy the Deputy Commissioner as to the genuineness of the claim so made. The appellants' petition filed on 18- 3-1993, undisputedly was not accompanied by any authoritative material disclosing their interest in the acquired land and in the amount awarded as compensation.

<u>21. The requirement of the law, as in section 28 of the Ordinance, being that within 45 days from the date of service of notice of the award under section 7(3) of the Ordinance person interested in the same is to file petition before the Arbitrator seeking revision of the award. Since no arbitration case was filed within the specified time by the person(s) who in the light of the revenue record was found interested in the award and that admittedly the appellants got their names mutated in the revenue record in 1997 and thereafter filed the arbitration case on 26-6-1997 as such, the High Court Division was not in error in holding that the arbitration case so filed was barred by limitation.</u>

<u>22. The other contention that appellants got their names mutated in the revenue record in 1997 and that immediately thereafter having had filed the arbitration case or, in other words, after mutation having had filed the arbitration case, within time prescribed in section 28 of the Ordinance the arbitration so filed was not barred by limitation is of no merit since law provides that person(s) interested in the award made under section 7(1) of the  Ordinance and that upon service of notice thereof in the light of the provision of section 7(3) of the Ordinance on the person(s) interested in the award is competent to file petition within the specified time before the Arbitrator seeking revision of the award. As because the appellants' names were not in the revenue record or in the record of the Deputy Commissioner when the award was made and the notice thereupon was served, consequently, under the law they were not required to be considered interested in the award made in respect of the land acquired. The scheme of the law relating to consideration of the objection of the interested person and thereupon making of award is confirmed to in respect of the person whose name appears in the revenue record or in the record of Deputy Commissioner on the date when the notice under section 3 of the Ordinance was served and thereafter on completion, of process as in sections 4 and 5 of the Ordinance notice under section 6 was served and that at the stage of enquiry under section 7(1) person whose name was in the revenue record or in the record of the Deputy Commissioner when the notice under section 6 of the Ordinance was served as well as others found interested in the land acquired such person would be competent to take exception or, in other words, objection to the award made and to file application before the Arbitrator seeking revision. There is no scope or occasion to enlarge the time specified in section 28 of the Ordinance on any pretext or, in other words, as contended in the instant case that Arbitration case was filed within 45 days from the date of mutation in 1997. Since appellants names were not in the revenue record or in the record of the Deputy Commissioner at the stages as stated hereinbefore and that when the award was made and the notice thereof was served and consequently, they were not competent to take exception to the award of compensation or, in other words, competent to file petition before the Arbitrator seeking revision of the award.</u>

23. But in a case where after service of notice under section 6 of the Ordinance if a person interested in the property does not represent to the Deputy Commissioner about the nature of interest in the property and the amount as well as particulars of the claim to compensation to such interest and that because of such non-representation notice under section 7(3) is not served on him, in such situation if the person interested in the property and the compensation awarded files Arbitration case, as provided by the provision of section 28 of the Ordinance seeking revision of the award within 45 days from the date of service of notice under section 7(3), as in the instant case was required from 24-4-1993, in that case the Arbitration case, subject to establishment of interest in the land acquired, would be maintainable.

24. In the background of the discussions made hereinbefore, in our opinion, as the appellants were not the interested persons when the compensation was made and the notice thereof was served, as such the arbitration case filed by the appellants after the expiry of the period, as provided by the law, the arbitration case was undoubtedly barred by limitation and the period of limitation prescribed being not extendable in any situation, the appellants upon mutating their names in the revenue record in 1997 were not competent to file the arbitration case or, in other words, the Arbitration case so filed was incompetent being barred by limitation.

25. In view of the opinion expressed hereinabove, we find no merit in the appeal.

26. Accordingly, the appeal is dismissed.

There is no order as to cost.

End.
